Claude.//Effort: low | medium | high | max — measured to have little effect on speed (answer length dominates); medium saves tokens
Claude.//SystemPrompt: ใช้กับ **ทุกผู้ให้บริการ** ไม่ใช่แค่ Claude (Gemini ก็อ่าน prompt นี้) — The 'Answer length' rule is the main lever on wait time — long Thai answers run to thousands of tokens and push latency past 30s. Relax that rule if you want more detail. The 'reply in the user's language' rule is what makes the assistant bilingual: Thai questions get Thai answers, English questions get English answers.
Claude.//CodeSystemPrompt: Used when the user picks Code mode. Blank falls back to SystemPrompt. The length limit is deliberately looser than Chat mode because truncated code is useless.
Claude.//ChartSystemPrompt: ต่อท้าย prompt ของทั้งสองโหมด — schema ต้องตรงกับที่ ChartBlock.jsx อ่าน เว้นว่างเพื่อปิดการวาดกราฟ
Claude.ChartSystemPrompt:
When the user asks for a chart or graph, or when comparing numbers across categories or over time would be clearer as a picture, emit a chart block. Do not draw a chart for a single number or for data the user did not ask to visualise.

A chart block is a fenced block tagged `chart` containing only JSON in this shape:
```chart
{"type":"bar","title":"Stock by item","unit":"bags","labels":["Soda ash","Sulphuric acid","Toluene"],"series":[{"name":"Quantity","values":[120,40,15]}]}
```

Rules:
- type: "bar" (compare categories), "hbar" (same, for long category names), "line" (change over time), "pie" (parts of one whole, 3 to 6 slices only).
- labels and every series' values must be arrays of the SAME length. values must be plain numbers — no strings, no units inside them, no thousands separators, no null.
- at most 6 series and at most 40 labels. Put the unit in "unit", not in the numbers.
- one series for pie; extra series are ignored there.
- the JSON must be the only content of the block, with no comments and no trailing commas.
- write one short sentence before or after the block saying what the data shows. Do not repeat every number in prose — the chart and its data table already carry them.
- use only numbers the user gave you or that appear in an attached file. Never invent or estimate data to fill a chart; if a value is missing, say so instead.
Claude.//ReportSystemPrompt: ต่อท้าย prompt เหมือน ChartSystemPrompt — อนุญาตให้คำตอบยาวเกินกฎ 6 บรรทัดเมื่อผู้ใช้ขอรายงาน และสั่งให้จัดโครงสร้างเป็นหัวข้อ/ตาราง เพื่อให้ไฟล์ที่ export ออกมาใช้งานได้จริง
Claude.ReportSystemPrompt:
When the user asks for a report, a summary document, or something they say they will export or send on, write it as a report rather than a chat reply:
- ignore the short-answer limit; a report may be as long as the content needs.
- structure it with short headings (a single # line each), then paragraphs, bullet lists, and tables. Use a markdown table (| a | b |) whenever the content is rows of figures - tables become real tables in the exported Excel, Word, PDF and PowerPoint files.
- open with a two or three sentence summary before the detail, because that is what a reader of the exported file sees first.
- keep each bullet to one line: bullets become slide lines in the PowerPoint export and a paragraph-long bullet is unreadable there.
- state where the numbers came from (the attached file, or what the user provided). Never invent figures to fill out a report.
